caption: United States v. Nora
canonical_case_name: United States v. Johnny Casel Nora
identity_method: MCP SEARCH-first (0 REST); cluster resolved from citation 765 F.3d 1049 (count=1); canonical_name_match + expected_citation_found both true
holding: Warrantless arrest effected by surrounding a home with 20-30 armed officers and ordering the occupant out over a PA system violates Payton absent exigency; where the perimeter is complete and all exits monitored, no flight/danger exigency justifies dispensing with the warrant (765 F.3d at 1055).

pincites.1055: perimeter defeats flight/danger exigency; distinguishes Al-Azzawy 784 F.2d at 894

caption: United States v. Al-Azzawy
canonical_case_name: United States v. Riad Abed Al-Azzawy
identity_method: MCP SEARCH-first (0 REST); cluster resolved from citation 784 F.2d 890; distinct from earlier 768 F.2d 1141 (1985, docket 84-5367)
holding: A suspect surrounded in his home and ordered out at bullhorn who emerges only under extreme coercion is arrested inside his residence (arrest location = suspect's position); the coerced emergence does not convert an in-home arrest into a public one (784 F.2d at 894-95). (Court affirmed arrest-was-inside but reversed suppression on exigency.)

caption: United States v. Vaneaton
canonical_case_name: United States v. Jack Palmer Vaneaton
identity_method: MCP SEARCH-first (0 REST); cluster resolved from citation 49 F.3d 1423 (count=1); lead opinion 9487908 (Trott, J.), dissent 9487909 (Tashima, J.)
holding: A suspect who voluntarily opens his door in response to a noncoercive knock and exposes himself to arrest is not protected by Payton; the dispositive question is voluntary exposure, not inside/outside the threshold (49 F.3d at 1426-27).

pincites.1427: voluntary opening in response to noncoercive knock; distinguishes Al-Azzawy at 895
